outcome: No unconditional progress on the base-a Wieferich prime infinitude question was found since 26 January 2024; the only developments are conditional results on the complementary non-Wieferich question (assuming the abc conjecture) and a number-field analogue, neither of which changes the stated rational-integer statement.
summary: The bullet, as Wikipedia words it, asks whether for a fixed integer a > 0 there are infinitely many primes p with a^(p-1) ≡ 1 (mod p^2) — i.e. infinitely many base-a Wieferich primes (the exponent 'a^p − 1' in the extracted statement is Wikipedia's own rendering of a^(p−1) − 1; this is the standard base-a Wieferich prime definition per the Wieferich prime Wikipedia article and Fermat quotient article, and matches the triage's reading). This remains completely open: for base 2, only the two Wieferich primes 1093 and 3511 are known, and exhaustive search (last reported up to 6.7×10^15, a pre-2024 result) has found no others; no new Wieferich prime for any small base was reported as discovered in the 2024-2026 window. The only related developments found in the window are: (1) Graves & Weiss (arXiv 2503.19144, March 2025) and Fellini/related work culminating in arXiv 2508.08472 (Aug 2025), which prove — conditional on the abc conjecture (or Masser's number-field abc-conjecture) — that there are infinitely many base-a NON-Wieferich primes, in the classical and number-field settings respectively. These address the complementary question (primes where the congruence fails) and are conditional, so under §3.1 and §6.1 they are not a change to this problem's status: they neither settle nor narrow the stated infinitude-of-Wieferich-primes question, and even if they addressed the same object they would only support 'claimed' at best, not a real status change, since they are conditional on an open conjecture. No unconditional result, no computational discovery of a new Wieferich prime, and no AI-related work touching this specific question were found. I therefore agree with the triage's verdict of 'none' and its classification of the found papers as adjacent/conditional rather than resolving.
competing_reading: One could argue the conditional abc-conjecture results deserve a 'progress' status with ai_role none, on the theory that they represent movement in the surrounding theory even though they attack the complementary (non-Wieferich) question. I reject this because per §3.1 a 'related problem' (here, a different congruence direction, and conditional on an unproven hypothesis) does not count as scope for this bullet; the stated question about Wieferich primes themselves has seen no bound move, no case settled, and no conditional resolution offered anywhere in the literature I found.
what_would_settle_it: An unconditional proof (or disproof) that infinitely many base-a Wieferich primes exist for some or all a, or a new explicit Wieferich prime discovered by computer search extending the known range beyond 6.7×10^15, would count as progress or resolution.
